items.claim: these nest boxes increase fledgling counts

cases.text: One: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 3 March, measured by 27 June, fledged 14 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Two: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 4 March, measured by 28 June, fledged 11 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Three: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 5 March, measured by 29 June, fledged 16 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Four: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 6 March, measured by 30 June, fledged 9 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.

items.passage:
A monitoring log records four plots where the same nest boxes were installed.
One: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 3 March, measured by 27 June, fledged 14 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Two: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 4 March, measured by 28 June, fledged 11 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Every box stood deep inside the reserve, beyond the range these birds forage. Prey abundance on the surrounding farmland ran a third above the previous year's. Counts cover every installed box, up all season or not, and a fifth of each plot's boxes went up mid-season.
Three: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 5 March, measured by 29 June, fledged 16 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Four: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 6 March, measured by 30 June, fledged 9 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.
Ring numbers and box references were filed with the monitoring register under standard warden codes.
items.notes: Check that all four cases carry one distinct value on reserve, species, season and warden. The closer neutralises the year-over-year comparison by holding food supply, weather and predator control fixed, which is what makes a before/after count adequate. Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_false.

items.confound_note: All four plots sit on one reserve, with one species in one spring under one warden, and the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: prey abundance on the surrounding farmland ran a third above the previous year's, an alternative cause of higher fledgling counts. The scope clause beside that fact puts every box at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range, placing the extra food over every brood that was counted. Each plot is measured against the same reserve a year earlier rather than against an unboxed wood in the same spring, and nothing in the evidence separates the boxes from the prey level. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the tally covering the whole set of installed boxes, adding no second defect.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. The prey peak works as a single confound precisely because the four plots share one reserve, one wood and one season, so one food-supply fact explains all four. Check that the closer reuses the TRUE closer's vocabulary (prey abundance, previous year, breeding-season weather, unchanged) so the difference is logical rather than lexical.

A monitoring log records four plots where the same nest boxes were installed.
One: pied flycatchers at Hollowmere reserve, boxed 3 June, measured by 27 March, fledged 14 more young than the same reserve in the previous spring; recorded by Trask.

items.confound_note: In cases one, three and four the fledgling count was recorded before the boxes went up: 27 March precedes 3 June at Hollowmere, and 24 September precedes 2 November at Brackenfen. Three quarters of the evidence therefore describes young that had already fledged when the boxes were installed, so it cannot be evidence for the boxes. The two remaining cases, Cransley and Vanehead, are not enough on their own.
items.notes: The closing sentence is identical to both TRUE items; the flaw lives entirely in the dates inside cases one and three, where the month tokens are swapped between installation and count so the bag of words is unchanged. Check that only the dates differ from diverse_true, and that no shared confound is available: four reserves across four seasons share no food supply or weather history.
